Hi Alex — quick answers & pointers ahead of the deep dive:

Embeddings + rerank pattern:
- The TS sample shows the common pattern: 1) compute embeddings (batching), 2) run an approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) filter (we include a small example using Faiss in the sample), 3) send top-N candidates into a reranker call that scores with the same or larger LM. The SDK gives primitives for embedding generation and model scoring; the sample wires them together end-to-end.

Structured output / tool calling:
- The SDK supports tool / function calling; you can register tools and the model will return a structured JSON that maps to your schema. The TS sample includes a simple tool that extracts invoice fields and returns a JSON payload you can consume directly in the frontend.

Auth & local testing:
- Two supported patterns: API key (good for quickstarts and short-term POC) or OIDC service account for production/private deployments. For local testing we recommend setting REDWOOD_API_KEY in your env:
  - export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<your-api-key>"  (mac/linux)
  - setx REDWOOD_API_KEY "<your-api-key>" (Windows PowerShell)
- For OIDC we provide a config example in the sample app (service-account.json + rwidew_config) and instructions for exchanging a short-lived token.

Routing, latency, and model selection:
- For 95p <200ms we typically recommend: low-latency model family (quantized variant for cost vs performance), dedicated pool or hosted with guaranteed throughput, and a smart routing policy that prefers the low-latency variant but fails over to a cheaper model if capacity constrained. The sample's routing config (routing.json) demonstrates a canary route and fallback to a cheaper family.

Attachments in this thread include the TS sample and an env checklist. For the deep dive I'll plan to demonstrate the sample app end-to-end and show how to run locally (node/npm) and in a staging VPC.

If you can confirm the deep dive time I'll prepare a short slide with architecture options and a checklist for Private vs Dedicated deployment.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
